title: Seats, holders and vacancies in the annual listings of boards and commissions
question: How many seats do the Clerk's annual listings show, how many are vacant or past their term, and how many people sit on more than one body?
finding: The 2025 listing shows 731 seats on 83 bodies: 598 holder names, 269 printed "VACANT", 140 printed "Holdover" and 117 printed "Term Expired"; 558 different people, 32 of them on two or more bodies. The 2026 listing shows 740 seats on 83 bodies: 596 holder names, 259 printed "VACANT", 107 printed "Holdover" and 86 printed "Term Expired"; 553 different people, 33 of them on two or more bodies. 417 people appear in both listings.
how: The three PDF listings are read as laid-out text. A seat is a line that begins with a seat number; holder names, "VACANT", "Holdover" and "Term Expired" are read from the "Seat Holder" column of each body's table. A seat printed vacant with a holdover member counts in both columns.
limits: The text reading misses some holders whose names wrap across several lines, and counts a seat whose line carries no number as missing; the counts are approximate (within a few percent). Officials who sit ex officio (department heads, supervisors) are counted like other holders. A holder past the term end may serve until a successor is appointed.

sources.t: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, Clerk of the Board: annual listing of boards and commissions (Maddy Act), 2025 (two parts) and 2026
